facts.statement: Masillastrix lived during the Middle Eocene.
Masillastrix is an extinct genus of stem‑owl known from the mid‑Eocene Messel Pit of Germany.
facts.quote: Masillastrix () is an extinct genus of stem-owl known from the mid-Eocene (Lutetian age) Messel Pit of Germany.

facts.statement: The specimen preserves the first owl fossil with well‑preserved feathers on the tail and wings.
facts.quote: This specimen is the first owl fossil with well-preserved feathers from the tail and wings.

facts.statement: Gerald Mayr and colleagues formally described Masillastrix blattophaga as a new genus and species in 2026.
facts.quote: In 2026, Gerald Mayr and colleagues described Masillastrix blattophaga as a new genus and species of early owl based on these fossil remains

facts.statement: Masillastrix has a proportionally smaller humerus with a wider upper end than any living owl, a trait also seen in Ypresiglaux.
facts.quote: The humerus (upper arm bone) is proportionately smaller, and with a wider upper end, than in all extant (living) owls, similar to Ypresiglaux.

facts.statement: Its tarsometatarsus is short and robust, resembling that of the genus Minerva.
facts.quote: The tarsometatarsus is short and robust, like in Minerva.

facts.statement: The first and second toe claws are notably larger than those of the third and fourth toes, a characteristic of Protostrigidae.
facts.quote: The unguals (claws) of the first and second toes of Masillastrix are notably larger than the unguals of the third and fourth toes, a feature characteristic of members of the family Protostrigidae

facts.statement: All tail feathers are of similar length, unlike the rounded tail of modern owls, and none of the feathers show the barred pattern common in extant species.
facts.quote: The tail feathers all have a similar length, contrasting with extant owls, where the tail is rounded. None of the wing or tail feathers exhibit the barred pattern seen in most modern owls.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Masillastrix within the owl stem group, outside the crown group of modern owls, in an unresolved clade with Minerva and Oligostrix.
facts.quote: Masillastrix was recovered as part of the owl stem group (member of the Strigiformes outside of the smallest group including all modern owls), in an unresolved clade also including Minerva and Oligostrix.

facts.statement: Masillastrix is assigned to the family Protostrigidae within the class Aves.
The known fossil occurrence of Masillastrix dates to the Lutetian stage, about 48.07 to 41.03 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Lutetian to Lutetian (48.07 to 41.03 million years ago)
